title: Alma counsels Helaman
summary: Alma counsels his son Helaman to keep God’s commandments, remember the captivity of their fathers, and trust God through trials.

explicit_facts.text: Alma addresses Helaman as his son and counsels him to keep God’s commandments.
Alma says their fathers were in bondage and God delivered them in their afflictions.

unspecified_visual_details: The place and time of the counsel.

summary: Alma reports that the angel’s warning filled him with fear and amazement lest he be destroyed, and he fell to the earth and heard no more. He could not open his mouth or use his limbs for three days and three nights. His brethren heard further words from the angel that Alma did not hear.

title: Alma remembers his sins
summary: Alma recalls torment over his sins, his rebellion against God, his failure to keep God's commandments, and his having led many of God's children toward destruction. The thought of coming into God's presence fills him with horror.

explicit_facts.text: Alma says his soul was racked with torment over his sins.

Alma says he had led many of God's children toward destruction.
The thought of coming into God's presence racked Alma's soul with horror.

unspecified_visual_details: Alma's appearance, clothing, posture, and surroundings.

narration.text: But I was racked with eternal torment,
Yea, I did remember all my sins and iniquities,
the very thought of coming into the presence of my God did rack my soul with inexpressible horror.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: These verses recount Alma's past actions and inward experience; they do not describe him speaking aloud here. Alma qualifies “murdered” with “or rather led them away unto destruction.”
prohibited_inventions: Do not stage Alma's remembered actions as present events or depict victims, hell, God appearing, or a judgment scene.
Do not assign these words to Mormon as spoken dialogue.

title: Alma's thought and three days of torment
summary: Alma wishes he could be banished and cease to exist rather than stand before God to be judged. He is racked for three days and three nights.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Alma may appear distressed while experiencing the pain he describes.
unspecified_visual_details: Alma's physical position and surroundings are not specified.

narration.text: Oh, thought I, that I could be banished and become extinct both soul and body, that I might not be brought to stand in the presence of my God, to be judged of my deeds.
And now, for three days and for three nights was I racked, even with the pains of a damned soul.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Alma's wish and description of pain report inward experiences, not visible events of banishment, judgment, or damnation.

He speaks of repeated deliverance from bondage and captivity by everlasting power, even down to the present day, and urges Helaman to remember their captivity.
